title: PartFacts
description: Canonical, kernel-measured facts about the geometry produced by executing a printspec on a real CAD kernel (OpenCascade/OCCT via brepjs or cadquery). A part is one or more solids: `topology` and `massProperties` describe the whole result AGGREGATED over every solid (mass properties sum across solids; the bounding box encloses them all), and the optional `solids` array carries the same facts per individual solid when disjoint solids need to be told apart. PartFacts is an OUTPUT artifact produced by a closed-source engine that runs geometry; this schema only defines and validates the shape of that output and is versioned independently of the printspec document schema. Several correctness properties cannot be expressed in JSON Schema and are normative obligations on the engine -- see the "Engine requirements" section of docs/partfacts.md. Every numeric field documents its unit and a precision note describing how the value was measured and to what tolerance it should be trusted.

partfactsVersion.title: PartFacts version
partfactsVersion.description: PartFacts schema version this document conforms to. Tracks the partfacts/<version>/ hosted path and is independent of the printspec document schema version. A loader MUST read this field from the raw JSON and dispatch to the matching schema version BEFORE validating, so an unsupported version yields a clear "unsupported PartFacts version" error rather than a confusing const mismatch.

units.title: Units
units.description: The unit system every numeric field in this document is expressed in. Fixed for 0.1.0 but recorded explicitly and required so consumers never have to assume.

length.title: Length unit
length.description: Linear unit for all length, area, volume, and coordinate fields. Millimeters only in 0.1.0. Derived units follow: area is mm^2, volume is mm^3, and the inertia tensor is mm^5 (see inertiaTensor).

angle.title: Angle unit
angle.description: Angular unit for any angle-valued field. Degrees only in 0.1.0.

massProperties.title: Mass properties (aggregate)
massProperties.description: Mass properties aggregated over every solid in the result. Required whenever topology.valid is true (see the top-level conditional); when topology.valid is false the shape is geometrically unsound and integrated quantities such as volume and inertia are undefined, so this section MAY be omitted. See MassProperties.

solids.title: Per-solid facts
solids.description: Optional per-solid breakdown, one entry per solid in the result, for when disjoint solids (for example a composable_part that produced more than one body) must be told apart. Each entry carries that single solid's own `topology` and, when meaningful, its own `massProperties`. This is an UNORDERED set: consumers MUST match solids by geometry (for example bounding box within tolerance), never by array index. The top-level `topology`/`massProperties` remain the aggregate source of truth and MUST agree with these entries (counts sum; mass properties sum).

extensions.title: Extensions
extensions.description: Extensible, forward-compatible section for later PartFacts tiers (for example manufacturability metrics, thin-wall maps, draft analysis, or mesh statistics) that are not part of the 0.1.0 core. Keys are namespaced tier or vendor identifiers; values are arbitrary. Consumers MUST ignore keys they do not recognize, and a new key here is an additive change that never requires a new PartFacts version.

allOf.title: massProperties required unless the shape is invalid

Vector3.title: Vector3
Vector3.description: An ordered triple in the part's local coordinate frame. Interpreted as a position, direction, or extent depending on the field that uses it; components carry that field's unit and precision.

UnitVector3.title: UnitVector3
UnitVector3.description: A direction in the part's local frame. Unit: dimensionless. Precision: components should describe a normalized vector (length ~1.0 within 1e-6); consumers should re-normalize before use rather than assuming exactness.

AxisAlignedBoundingBox.title: Axis-aligned bounding box
AxisAlignedBoundingBox.description: The part's axis-aligned bounding box (AABB) in its local frame. Unit: mm. Precision: kernel BoundingBox result, exact to kernel tolerance (~1e-7 mm) for planar/linear extents; curved surfaces may be reported to a small positive tessellation margin, so treat the AABB as a tight outer bound, not an exact silhouette.

min.title: Min corner
min.description: Minimum (x, y, z) corner, in mm.

max.title: Max corner
max.description: Maximum (x, y, z) corner, in mm.

size.title: Size
size.description: Extent along each axis (max - min), in mm. Redundant with min/max and provided for convenience; when present it must equal max - min within tolerance.

Provenance.title: Provenance
Provenance.description: Where this PartFacts document came from: which printspec version described the part, which engine and CAD kernel executed it, and the exact container image that ran, so a result is reproducible and auditable.

printspecVersion.title: printspec version
printspecVersion.description: Version of the printspec document schema the executed spec declared (its printspecVersion), for example "0.2.0".

specDigest.title: Spec digest
specDigest.description: Optional digest of the exact printspec document that was executed, formatted "sha256:<64 hex>". It MUST be the SHA-256 of the document's RFC 8785 (JSON Canonicalization Scheme) canonical form, so independent TypeScript and Python implementations produce the same digest for the same spec. Lets a consumer confirm these facts belong to a specific spec and use the digest as a stable cache key.

generator.title: Generator
generator.description: The printspec generator that emitted the kernel program (for example the brepjs or cadquery generator), with its version.

kernel.title: CAD kernel
kernel.description: The geometry kernel that executed the program and measured these facts (for example OpenCascade/OCCT), with its version.

imageDigest.title: Image digest
imageDigest.description: Content-addressable digest of the container image that ran the kernel, formatted as "sha256:<64 hex>" (an OCI image digest). Pins the exact runtime for reproducibility.

generatedAt.title: Generated at
generatedAt.description: Optional RFC 3339 timestamp for when the kernel produced these facts.

NamedVersion.title: Named version
NamedVersion.description: A named software component and its version string.

version.title: Version
version.description: Version string as reported by the component, for example a semver or an upstream release tag.

Topology.title: Topology
Topology.description: Boundary-representation (B-rep) topology and validity of the shape, from a BRepCheck-style analysis. All counts are exact non-negative integers (unit: count). The flags summarize kernel checks and are the first thing a downstream rule should gate on: mass properties and the feature inventory are only trustworthy when the shape is valid and closed.

solidCount.title: Solid count
solidCount.description: Number of solids in the result. Unit: count (exact). A well-formed single part is 1; 0 means the program produced no solid; >1 means a compound of disjoint solids (each described in the optional top-level `solids` array).

shellCount.title: Shell count
shellCount.description: Number of shells (connected face sets bounding the solids). Unit: count (exact).

faceCount.title: Face count
faceCount.description: Number of faces (bounded surfaces) in the B-rep. Unit: count (exact).

edgeCount.title: Edge count
edgeCount.description: Number of edges (bounded curves) in the B-rep. Unit: count (exact).

vertexCount.title: Vertex count
vertexCount.description: Number of vertices (points) in the B-rep. Unit: count (exact).

closed.title: Closed
closed.description: Whether every shell is watertight (closed), i.e. no free boundary edges. A closed shell is required for meaningful volume and inertia.

manifold.title: Manifold
manifold.description: Whether the shape is manifold: every edge is shared by exactly two faces, with no non-manifold vertices or edges. Non-manifold shapes are usually not printable and make mass properties unreliable.

valid.title: Valid
valid.description: Overall BRepCheck-style verdict: true only when the kernel's shape analyzer reports no errors across all sub-shapes. A convenience roll-up of checks (a subset of which are itemized in checks). When false, checks is required so the failure is actionable.

genus.title: Genus
genus.description: Optional topological genus (number of through-handles/holes in the surface) of a closed manifold solid. Unit: count (exact). Omitted when not computed or not well-defined.

maxShapeTolerance.title: Max shape tolerance
maxShapeTolerance.description: Optional health metric: the maximum per-subshape tolerance across all vertices, edges, and faces of the shape. Unit: mm. OCCT per-subshape tolerances balloon after boolean operations; a shape can be valid:true yet geometrically mushy. A typical clean value is ~1e-7 mm; a large value (for example ~1e-2 mm) flags a shape that will tessellate, slice, and compare poorly even though it passed validity. TODO(tolerance): the threshold above which consumers should treat a shape as degraded is not yet fixed.

checks.title: Validity checks
checks.description: Optional itemized BRepCheck-style findings, so a consumer can see which specific checks passed or failed rather than only the rolled-up valid flag. Required when valid is false. This is an UNORDERED set: consumers MUST match findings by their `name`, never by array index.

allOf.title: checks required when the shape is invalid

ValidityCheck.title: Validity check
ValidityCheck.description: One named check from a BRepCheck-style analysis and its result.

name.title: Check name
name.description: Identifier of the check, for example "self-intersection", "free-edges", "small-edge", "invalid-orientation", or "closed-shell".

status.title: Status
status.description: Result of the check. "warn" flags a non-fatal anomaly that still leaves valid true.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: Optional human-readable explanation of the finding.

SolidFacts.title: Solid facts
SolidFacts.description: Facts for a single solid within a multi-solid result. Carries that solid's own topology and, when the solid is geometrically sound, its own mass properties (omitted when that solid's topology.valid is false, mirroring the top-level rule).

id.title: Solid id
id.description: Optional within-document identifier for this solid. Like all ids in PartFacts it is NOT portable across kernels; match solids by geometry for cross-kernel comparison.

topology.title: Topology
topology.description: This single solid's topology (solidCount is 1 for a well-formed entry).

massProperties.title: Mass properties
massProperties.description: This single solid's mass properties. Omit when this solid's topology.valid is false.

MassProperties.title: Mass properties
MassProperties.description: Geometric mass properties computed by the kernel assuming uniform unit density (so "mass" is proportional to volume; these are shape properties, not material weights). At the top level these AGGREGATE over every solid (volume, surface area, and inertia sum; the center of mass is the volume-weighted centroid; the bounding box encloses all solids). Only meaningful when the corresponding topology.closed and topology.valid are true. Precision notes are per field; in general the kernel integrates these numerically and they are exact for planar/prismatic geometry and accurate to a small tolerance for curved geometry.

volume.title: Volume
volume.description: Enclosed volume. Unit: mm^3. Precision: kernel volume integration; exact to kernel tolerance (~1e-6 relative) for prismatic geometry, with a small numerical margin for curved surfaces. 0 indicates a degenerate or non-solid result. At the top level this is the sum over all solids.

surfaceArea.title: Surface area
surfaceArea.description: Total area of all boundary faces. Unit: mm^2. Precision: kernel surface integration; ~1e-6 relative for planar faces, small numerical margin for curved faces. At the top level this is the sum over all solids.

centerOfMass.title: Center of mass
centerOfMass.description: Centroid under uniform density, in the part's local frame. Unit: mm. Precision: derived from the same volume integration as volume; ~1e-6 mm for prismatic geometry. At the top level this is the volume-weighted centroid over all solids.

boundingBox.title: Axis-aligned bounding box
boundingBox.description: The axis-aligned bounding box. At the top level it encloses every solid. See AxisAlignedBoundingBox for unit and precision.

inertiaTensor.title: Inertia tensor
inertiaTensor.description: Mass moment-of-inertia tensor about the center of mass. See InertiaTensor for unit, reference point, and precision.

InertiaTensor.title: Inertia tensor
InertiaTensor.description: Symmetric 3x3 mass moment-of-inertia tensor. Unit: mm^5 (second moment of volume under uniform unit density; multiply by material density in kg/mm^3 to obtain kg*mm^2). Reference: taken about the center of mass, aligned to the local frame axes, unless referencePoint says otherwise. Precision: kernel integration, same tolerance class as volume. Only the six independent components are stored (Ixy = Iyx, etc.).

ixx.title: Ixx
ixx.description: Second moment about the X axis. Unit: mm^5.

iyy.title: Iyy
iyy.description: Second moment about the Y axis. Unit: mm^5.

izz.title: Izz
izz.description: Second moment about the Z axis. Unit: mm^5.

ixy.title: Ixy
ixy.description: XY product of inertia. Unit: mm^5.

ixz.title: Ixz
ixz.description: XZ product of inertia. Unit: mm^5.

iyz.title: Iyz
iyz.description: YZ product of inertia. Unit: mm^5.

referencePoint.title: Reference point
referencePoint.description: Optional point the tensor is taken about, in mm, in the local frame. Omitted means the center of mass.

FeatureInventory.title: Feature inventory
FeatureInventory.description: A classified inventory of the boundary faces, so downstream checks can find holes, bosses, and walls without re-running a kernel. 0.1.0 enumerates the two classes that matter most for printed parts -- cylindrical faces (holes, bores, pins) and planar faces (walls, floors, mounting faces) -- plus an optional derived grouping of co-axial cylindrical faces into logical holes. Faces the classifier does not place in a listed class are counted in otherFaceCount. Every geometric field carries mm units and a precision note on its own definition.

cylindricalFaces.title: Cylindrical faces
cylindricalFaces.description: Every face lying on a cylindrical surface, each described by its axial endpoints, radius, and handedness, plus whether it passes through the part. Lets a rule locate holes and check their diameters. This is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for cylindrical geometry and an UNORDERED set: consumers MUST match faces by geometry (axis + radius + axial extent within tolerance), never by array index. One physical hole can appear as several faces here (a bore through two walls, a counterbore's two radii, or a cylinder split by an intersecting feature); the optional `holes` array groups those into logical features.

planarFaces.title: Planar faces
planarFaces.description: Every planar face, each described by its outward normal, signed plane offset, and area. Lets a rule find walls, floors, and mounting faces and reason about wall areas and offsets. This is an UNORDERED set: consumers MUST match faces by geometry (normal + offset + area within tolerance), never by array index.

holes.title: Logical holes
holes.description: Optional derived grouping of co-axial cylindrical faces into logical features, so a "is there a 6mm through-bore" or hole-count check gets one answer instead of several half-answers. Each entry merges the faces that share a `featureId` into one feature with ordered radial `segments` (so a counterbore's two radii are representable). This array is DERIVED from cylindricalFaces and MUST agree with it (cylindricalFaces remains the source of truth); it is an UNORDERED set, matched by geometry, not index.

otherFaceCount.title: Other face count
otherFaceCount.description: Number of boundary faces not classified as cylindrical or planar (for example conical, spherical, toroidal, or general spline faces). Unit: count (exact). cylindricalFaces + planarFaces + otherFaceCount should equal topology.faceCount.

CylindricalFace.title: Cylindrical face
CylindricalFace.description: A face on a cylindrical surface -- the wall of a hole, bore, or pin. Located by its two axial endpoints (start, end). Handedness (a concave inner bore versus a convex outer boss) is given by the required `convex` flag, which distinguishes a hole from a pin of the same radius.

id.title: Face id
id.description: Optional within-document identifier for this face (for example a kernel sub-shape index), referenced by hole segments' faceIds. It is a within-document reference ONLY: it is NOT stable across kernels or across kernel versions and MUST NOT be used for cross-kernel matching.

featureId.title: Feature id
featureId.description: Optional grouping key: cylindrical faces that belong to the same logical hole (co-axial within tolerance) share this value, and a matching entry appears in featureInventory.holes. Like `id`, this is a within-document reference and is NOT portable across kernels.

radius.title: Radius
radius.description: Cylinder radius. Unit: mm. Precision: exact to kernel tolerance (~1e-7 mm) -- read from the analytic surface, not tessellation. Diameter is 2 x radius.

axis.title: Axis direction
axis.description: Direction of the cylinder axis in the local frame, as a convenience equal to normalize(end - start). Unit: dimensionless (normalized). MUST be consistent with the endpoints within tolerance.

start.title: Start point
start.description: One endpoint of the face's axial extent, in mm, in the local frame. Engine requirement: start/end MUST be derived from the face's parametric bounds, not from the cylindrical surface's stored origin (which has no defined relationship to the face and differs between kernels). Precision: ~1e-6 mm.

end.title: End point
end.description: The other endpoint of the face's axial extent, in mm, in the local frame. See start for the parametric-bounds requirement. Precision: ~1e-6 mm.

length.title: Axial length
length.description: Axial extent of the cylindrical face. Unit: mm. Equal to |end - start| and MUST be consistent with the endpoints within tolerance. For a straight drilled hole this is the hole depth.

through.title: Through
through.description: Optional: true if the hole passes entirely through the part (open at both ends of this face's run), false if it is blind (terminates inside the solid). Determined by the engine from the surrounding topology. When ABSENT it means unknown -- a consumer MUST treat an absent value as unknown, never as false.

convex.title: Convex
convex.description: Required handedness: true if the material is outside the cylinder (a convex boss/pin), false if the material surrounds a void (a concave hole/bore). This distinguishes a 4mm hole from a 4mm pin and is more reliably computable than `through`.

blindDepth.title: Blind depth
blindDepth.description: Optional depth from the opening to the bottom of a blind hole. Unit: mm. Precision: ~1e-6 mm. Present only when through is false and the depth is known; typically equals length.

Hole.title: Logical hole
Hole.description: One logical hole: the merge of all co-axial cylindrical faces sharing a featureId, with its radial profile expressed as ordered segments along the axis. Derived from cylindricalFaces and MUST agree with them.

featureId.title: Feature id
featureId.description: The shared grouping key; matches the featureId on every cylindrical face that composes this hole. Within-document only; NOT portable across kernels.

axis.title: Axis direction
axis.description: Direction of the hole axis, equal to normalize(end - start). Unit: dimensionless (normalized).

start.title: Start point
start.description: Axial start of the whole feature (the extreme endpoint along -axis), in mm.

end.title: End point
end.description: Axial end of the whole feature (the extreme endpoint along +axis), in mm.

through.title: Through
through.description: Optional: true if the merged feature passes entirely through the part. When ABSENT it means unknown; a consumer MUST NOT treat an absent value as false. This resolves the split-face problem where each face alone looked blind.

convex.title: Convex
convex.description: Handedness of the feature: false for a concave hole/bore, true for a convex boss/pin. Matches the convex flag of its faces.

segments.title: Segments
segments.description: The hole's radial profile as segments ORDERED along the axis from start to end, so a counterbore (a wide segment then a narrow segment) is representable. Unlike the other arrays, this array's order is significant.

HoleSegment.title: Hole segment
HoleSegment.description: One constant-radius run of a logical hole, referencing the cylindrical face(s) it came from.

radius.title: Radius
radius.description: Radius of this run. Unit: mm.

start.title: Start point
start.description: Axial start of this run, in mm.

end.title: End point
end.description: Axial end of this run, in mm.

faceIds.title: Face ids
faceIds.description: The `id` values of the cylindrical face(s) that make up this run. Within-document references only; NOT portable across kernels.

PlanarFace.title: Planar face
PlanarFace.description: A flat face -- a wall, floor, lid, or mounting surface. Fully located by its outward normal and signed plane offset.

id.title: Face id
id.description: Optional within-document identifier for this face (for example a kernel sub-shape index). It is a within-document reference ONLY: it is NOT stable across kernels or across kernel versions and MUST NOT be used for cross-kernel matching.

normal.title: Outward normal
normal.description: Outward-pointing surface normal in the local frame. Unit: dimensionless (normalized). Engine requirement: the outward sense MUST account for the face's TopAbs_REVERSED orientation; ignoring it inverts roughly half of all normals (and still passes smoke tests on symmetric parts).

offset.title: Plane offset
offset.description: Signed distance from the local origin to the face's plane along `normal`. Unit: mm. The supporting plane is { p : dot(normal, p) = offset }. Together with normal this fully locates the plane, so wall-thickness and offset checks are always possible. Precision: ~1e-6 mm.

area.title: Area
area.description: Area of the face. Unit: mm^2. Precision: kernel surface integration; exact for polygonal faces (~1e-6 relative), small numerical margin when the outer or inner boundary is curved.

centroid.title: Centroid
centroid.description: Optional area centroid of the face, in mm, in the local frame. Precision: ~1e-6 mm.
